Stimulus protocol

PYTHON

Write a sequence, then run it on the rig. grating(...) or bar(...) presents a stimulus; blank(duration) inserts a gray interval. Durations are seconds.

Available stimulus parameters

grating(orientation=0, duration=1, spatial_frequency=5, temporal_frequency=2, phase=0, x=0, y=0, size=0.9)

Orientation describes bar angle (0° = horizontal). Phase is in degrees. Spatial frequency is cycles per screen height. Position and size use screen half-height units; x spans −1.5…1.5 and y spans −1…1.

Ordinary Python loops, lists, math and random can be used to build the sequence. This panel constructs a protocol before presentation; it is not the later data-analysis workspace. Maximum: 300 seconds / 1,000 segments.

One simulated neuron.

Explore: what makes the neuron fire?

Imagine an electrode is recording from a visual neuron. You can see its spikes in the voltage trace and hear them as clicks. Find a stimulus that makes the neuron respond strongly.

  • Start the webcam and turn on sound. Draw a black bar on white paper and hold it in front of the camera.
  • Explore position. Move the bar around the image and look for a sensitive region.
  • Explore orientation. Rotate the bar and listen for changes in the response.
  • Try different bar widths, lengths and movements. Keep other features steady so you can tell what matters.

Does the neuron respond everywhere? Which angle works best? Can you find a strong stimulus and a weak one?

Goal: figure out what makes this neuron fire.
